question: {If } tan theta = (1)/(2), { then } (cos theta - sin theta)/(sin theta + cos theta) { is equal to :}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take common cosθ:

(cosθ − sinθ)/(sinθ + cosθ)

= cosθ(1 − tanθ) / cosθ(tanθ + 1)

= (1 − tanθ)/(1 + tanθ)

Put tanθ = 1/2:

= (1 − 1/2)/(1 + 1/2) = (1/2)/(3/2) = 1/3

**∴ Answer = 1/3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tanθ = 1/2

**Formula used:**

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let sinθ = 1k, cosθ = 2k

⇒ Substitute:

(cosθ − sinθ)/(sinθ + cosθ)

= (2k − 1k)/(1k + 2k)

= k / 3k = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Key Identity

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ

Simplification Trick

Take common cosθ to convert into tan form

Alternative Approach

Assume sinθ and cosθ proportional to tan ratio

Quick Tip

Convert expression fully in terms of tanθ for easy substitution
